semantic_review.finding: Production composeSfInstallation uses public NodeHttpServerRequest.toIncomingMessage and NodeStream.fromReadable with closeOnDone:false/highWaterMark0. Request size checks happen per chunk before enqueue, including absent Content-Length. Header length is validated but never trusted for allocation. Abort/read-error/truncation terminate the body and release listeners/readers. The stream is lazy and singly consumed.

The command route consumes a bounded 65536-byte Uint8Array, then fatal UTF-8 and JSON validation before schema admission/dispatch. Exact-byte, multibyte, invalid/truncated and idempotency cases are in the source tests. Workbench and workbench-* delegated transports use the same 65536 boundary. Current other consumers retain their own smaller validators/body bounds.

Strict listener Host/origin and explicit Microsoft proxy are retained. Forwarded headers do not create identity; the same final Request flows through tested auth/admit/command/dispatch. Current entry72, local identity/contracts/store72 and application73 are retained. Private 400/413/503/no-store/nosniff and connection close apply at this boundary; no token logger or tracing relaxation is introduced.

The host runtime factory import moves into the trusted absolute installation loader. The local Node transport probe can import the bridge without the Bun-specific canonical domain graph. This is not a loader shim and does not prove complete Microsoft domain compatibility with Node24. Arbitrary owner-selected external factories require their own deployment closure.

Known good 98358-byte BMP goes through actual private SQLite/domain/CAS/audit and exact byte checks; corrupted bytes are rejected before effects by an explicit exact-digest scanner fixture. ClamD is not represented by this fixture. The known declared-CL16MiB vs contract25MiB mismatch remains held; default stream policy is finite, and explicit smaller supplied finite limits are tested. Broader trusted Procurement caps above16MiB are not qualified.

Actual planner/forecast/analysis/views handlers read their body before human/UI admission; same Workbench route transport budget bounds them. Procurement sourcing and dashboard67 already have bounded readers. Generic callbacks that ignore their request body may perform side effects before it is consumed; zero-write proof is limited to tested body-consuming commands/uploads. No blanket guarantee about every handler or all legacy reader locks is made.

The Bun raw TCP listener regression requires complete early413 JSON and remote EOF before the client sends EOF or destroys its socket. The Node24 probe destroys its client after response end, so its physical-close assertion alone does not prove server-initiated EOF. Node still establishes real Node transport response, size, identity and disconnect behavior; these scopes remain distinct.

Understated Content-Length defines the HTTP message boundary. The selected short-body malformed-JSON regression is not universal detection of extra pipelined bytes. CL parse errors, excess, truncation and actual streamed bytes are independently bounded.
